paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: Suppose the student union of your university is organizing an online discussion on interpersonal relationships. You are to write an essay on ways to maintain a warm and friendly relationship with your classmates and on the benefits of such a relationship. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：假设你所在大学的学生会正在组织一场关于人际关系的在线讨论。你要写一篇关于如何与同学保持热情友好的关系以及这种关系的好处的文章。您将有 30 分钟的时间来完成该任务。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear three news reports. At the end of each news report, you will hear two or three questions. Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A), B), C) and D). Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.

paragraphs.sourceText: You probably haven’t taken the time to think of all the work that went into creating the shirt on your back. I mean, how hard it could be to create fabric and 26 it into a shirt shape. Don’t machines do all that? Well, creating fabric from cotton, which is the most 27 clothing material, is actually a process that involves a lot of water, 2,700 liters per shirt to be 28 . Take a look at the video below from National Geographic for some more mind-blowing 29 about cotton clothing production.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您可能没有花时间思考制作您背上的衬衫所需的所有工作。我的意思是，制造布料并将其缝成衬衫形状是多么困难。难道这一切不是机器做的吗？嗯，用棉花这种最丰富的服装材料制造面料实际上是一个需要大量水的过程，准确地说，每件衬衫需要 2,700 升水。观看下面来自《国家地理》的视频，了解有关棉质服装生产的更多令人兴奋的统计数据。

paragraphs.sourceText: Clean water is 30 becoming one of the most sought-after resources in the world. Given how large the 31 and cotton industries are, they take up a lot of our fresh water demands across the world, according to The Huffington Post. The video from National Geographic was created to spread 32 of how environmentally harmful cotton is. But the situation can be made better. Through better water management and farming practices, water usage in cotton production can be cut down by 33 40 percent.
paragraphs.translationZh: 清洁水日益成为世界上最受欢迎的资源之一。据《赫芬顿邮报》报道，考虑到纺织和棉花工业的规模，它们占用了我们在世界各地的大量淡水需求。国家地理制作这段视频的目的是为了让人们认识到棉花对环境的危害性。但情况还可以变得更好。通过更好的水管理和农业实践，棉花生产的用水量可以减少近 40%。

paragraphs.sourceText: Called “Better Cotton”, this environmentally conscious product will save millions of liters of water a year simply from 34 the demands of cotton production. Cotton doesn’t have to go, since it is, after all, one of the most useful cash crops across the globe. However, as water supplies 35 , farmers and consumers need to be more conscious of the effect that these products have on the environment as a whole.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种环保产品被称为“更好的棉花”，仅通过减少棉花生产的需求即可每年节省数百万升水。棉花不必消失，因为它毕竟是全球最有用的经济作物之一。然而，随着供水减少，农民和消费者需要更加意识到这些产品对整个环境的影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Spoken Web
paragraphs.translationZh: 口语网络

paragraphs.sourceText: A) We’re growing more used to chatting to our computers, phones and smart speakers through voice assistants like Amazon’s Alexa, Apple’s Siri and Microsoft’s Cortana. Blind and partially sighted people have been using text-to-speech converters for decades.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答）我们越来越习惯通过亚马逊的 Alexa、苹果的 Siri 和微软的 Cortana 等语音助手与电脑、手机和智能音箱聊天。盲人和弱视人士几十年来一直在使用文本转语音转换器。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Out of these assistants, Siri is the most well-known. The assistant uses voice inquiries and a natural-language user interface (界面) to answer questions. The software adapts to users’ individual language usages, searches, and preferences, with continuing use.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 在这些助手中，Siri 是最知名的。助理使用语音查询和自然语言用户界面来回答问题。该软件会适应用户的个人语言使用、搜索和偏好，并持续使用。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Some think voice could soon take over from typing and clicking as the main way to interact online. But what are the challenges of moving to “the spoken web”?
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 一些人认为语音很快就会取代打字和点击成为在线互动的主要方式。但是转向“语音网络”的挑战是什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: D) What use is written online content if you can’t read? That is the situation facing illiterate (不识字) African farmers. They are often denied crucial information the web offers many others. With a literacy rate in some parts of Africa at only 22.6%, farmers are often “underpaid for their produce because they might be unaware of the prevailing prices,” says Francis Dittoh, a researcher behind Mr Meteo, a speech-based weather information service.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 如果你看不懂，那么网上写的内容有什么用？这就是不识字的非洲农民所面临的处境。他们常常无法获得网络提供的许多其他重要信息。基于语音的天气信息服务公司 Mr Meteo 的研究员弗朗西斯·迪托 (Francis Dittah) 表示，非洲某些地区的识字率仅为 22.6%，农民的农产品往往“报酬过低，因为他们可能不了解现行价格”。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) “The most frequently heard complaint is about rainfall predictions,” says Mr Dittoh, who lives in Tamale, northern Ghana. “They tell us the methods their forefathers used to predict the weather don’t seem to work as well these days.” This is down to climate change, he believes. Yet knowing when it’s going to rain is vital for farmers wanting to sow seeds, irrigate crops or take their animals out to the fields to feed on grass.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) “最常听到的抱怨是关于降雨预测的，”住在加纳北部塔马利的迪托先生说。 “他们告诉我们，他们的祖先用来预测天气的方法如今似乎不太管用了。”他认为，这归因于气候变化。然而，对于想要播种、灌溉农作物或将牲畜带到田里吃草的农民来说，知道什么时候会下雨至关重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Mr Dittoh says the idea of converting online weather reports into speech came from the farmers themselves, after a workshop in the village of Guabuligah. “They came up with this,” he says. Mr Meteo takes the online weather forecast, converts it to a short recording in the appropriate language and makes it available on a basic phone. Farmers ring up to receive the information. The local language Dagbani is spoken by 1.2 million people but is not served by any online translation applications. The service was designed to be cheap and easy to run, says Mr Ditto. He plans to begin field tests this month, working with Tamale’s Savanna Agricultural Research Institute.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 迪托先生表示，在瓜布利加村举办研讨会后，农民们自己提出了将在线天气预报转化为语音的想法。 “他们想出了这个，”他说。梅特奥先生获取在线天气预报，将其转换为适当语言的简短录音，并在普通手机上提供。农民们打电话来获取信息。当地语言达格巴尼语有 120 万人使用，但没有任何在线翻译应用程序提供服务。迪托先生表示，这项服务的设计初衷是价格低廉且易于运行。他计划本月与塔马利的稀树草原农业研究所合作开始实地测试。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) The spoken web could also help the one-in-five adults in Europe and the US with poor reading skills. But building the spoken web — web-to-voice and voice-to-web — isn’t straightforward. For software to understand pizza is served at Italian restaurants is easy. To cover multiple domains and to be able to have a conversation with users on every single topic is still a long way off.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 语音网络还可以帮助欧洲和美国五分之一的阅读能力较差的成年人。但构建语音网络（网络到语音和语音到网络）并不简单。对于软件来说，了解意大利餐厅供应的披萨是很容易的。要覆盖多个领域并能够就每个主题与用户进行对话还有很长的路要走。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) So although many computer assistants can answer simple questions about the weather and play music for us, anything resembling a wide-ranging human conversation is decades away. Artificial intelligence just isn’t smart enough yet. Even turning your voice into text — automatic speech recognition — is one of the hardest problems to solve, as there are as many ways to pronounce things as there are people on the planet.
paragraphs.translationZh: H）因此，尽管许多计算机助手可以回答有关天气的简单问题并为我们播放音乐，但任何类似于广泛的人类对话的技术还需要几十年的时间。人工智能还不够智能。即使将你的声音转换成文本（自动语音识别）也是最难解决的问题之一，因为地球上有多少人就有多少种发音方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Siri has often been praised for its ability to interpret our casual language and deliver very specific and accurate result, sometimes even providing additional information. But it is still somewhat restricted, particularly when the language moved away from stiffer commands into more human interactions. In one example, the phrase “Send a text to Jason, Clint, Sam, and Lee saying we’re having dinner at Silver Cloud restaurant” was interpreted as sending a message to Jason only, containing the text “Clint Sam and Lee saying we’re having dinner at Silver Cloud restaurant”. It has also been noted that Siri lacks a proper editing function, as saying “Edit message to say: we’re at Silver Cloud restaurant and you should come find us” generates “Clint Sam and Lee saying we’re having dinner at Silver Cloud restaurant to say we’re at Silver Cloud restaurant and you should come find us”.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) Siri 经常因其解释我们的随意语言并提供非常具体和准确的结果的能力而受到称赞，有时甚至提供额外的信息。但它仍然受到一定的限制，特别是当语言从更严格的命令转向更多的人际互动时。在一个示例中，短语“向 Jason、Clint、Sam 和 Lee 发送一条短信，说我们要在 Silver Cloud 餐厅吃晚饭”被解释为仅向 Jason 发送一条消息，其中包含文本“Clint Sam 和 Lee 说我们要在 Silver Cloud 餐厅吃晚饭”。人们还注意到，Siri 缺乏适当的编辑功能，比如说“编辑消息说：我们在银云餐厅，你应该来找我们”会生成“克林特·萨姆和李说我们在银云餐厅吃晚饭，说我们在银云餐厅，你应该来找我们”。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Using voice interaction feels far more intimate than surfing the net the old-fashioned way. This is intentional as the informal tone of the assistant helps create an emotional attachment. But if something speaks, it must also listen. Our phones are always near us and they are collecting data about us all the time. This has already raised privacy concerns. The American Civil Liberties Union has stated that digital assistants create a threat to privacy from hackers. Some people have other concerns. They worry assistants will one day be used to deliver advertising directly to us.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 使用语音交互比传统方式上网感觉更亲密。这是故意的，因为助理的非正式语气有助于建立情感依恋。但如果有东西说话，它也必须倾听。我们的手机总是在我们身边，它们一直在收集有关我们的数据。这已经引起了隐私问题。美国公民自由联盟表示，数字助理对黑客的隐私构成威胁。有些人还有其他担忧。他们担心有一天助理会被用来直接向我们投放广告。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) But digital voices need more personality to make them popular. Robots are not yet witty, Siri is boring. The benefits of using voice instead of tapping fingers obviously depend on the context. Doctors completing online forms about their patients by speech, for example, can dictate 150 words a minute, three times faster than typing on a keyboard. This enables them to spend less time on administration and more time with patients.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 但数字声音需要更多的个性才能使其流行。机器人还不够机智，Siri 很无聊。使用语音而不是敲击手指的好处显然取决于上下文。例如，医生通过语音填写有关患者的在线表格，每分钟可以听写 150 个单词，比键盘打字快三倍。这使他们能够花更少的时间在管理上，而将更多的时间花在患者身上。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Last year, speech recognition company Nuance helped a doctors’ surgery in Dukinfield, near Manchester, set up a speech system for the practice’s six doctors. Now they can dictate notes on a patient’s health condition and treatment and a smart assistant automatically enters the information into the right fields on a web form. Previously, the doctors made voice recordings that were then transcribed by secretaries — a process that was costly and likely to cause delays. The new system means letters to patients now have more detail.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 去年，语音识别公司 Nuance 帮助曼彻斯特附近杜金菲尔德的一家医生诊所为该诊所的六名医生建立了语音系统。现在，他们可以口述有关患者健康状况和治疗的注释，智能助手会自动将信息输入网络表单上的正确字段中。此前，医生先进行录音，然后由秘书转录——这一过程成本高昂，而且可能会导致延误。新系统意味着写给患者的信件现在有更多细节。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) Using voice also makes sense when you’re doing other things with your hands. Think about when you’re cooking, and you just want to know what the next step in the recipe is. Your hands are covered with oil; you’re not going to get on the iPad, so it’s a lot more natural to talk. And speech obviously makes sense when you’re driving. In the US, 29% of drivers admit they surf behind the wheel, according to insurance firm State Farm. This is up from 13% in 2009. No wonder using mobile phones while driving causes more crashes a year than drink driving, says the US National Safety Council.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 当您用手做其他事情时，使用声音也很有意义。想想当你做饭时，你只想知道食谱的下一步是什么。你的手沾满了油；你不需要使用 iPad，所以说话就更自然了。当你开车时，言语显然是有意义的。根据保险公司 State Farm 的数据，在美国，29% 的司机承认他们在开车时冲浪。这一数字比 2009 年的 13% 有所上升。美国国家安全委员会表示，开车时使用手机每年造成的车祸比酒后驾驶还要多也就不足为奇了。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. According to Francis Dittoh, their speech-based weather information service was meant to be inexpensive and easy to use.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 据弗朗西斯·迪托称，他们基于语音的天气信息服务应该价格低廉且易于使用。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Using voice instead of typing enables doctors to spend more time taking care of patients.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 使用语音代替打字使医生能够花更多时间照顾病人。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. It is extremely difficult to convert voice into text because of different pronunciations.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 由于发音不同，将语音转换为文本极其困难。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. African farmers unable to read often don’t have access to important information conveyed online.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 不识字的非洲农民往往无法获取网上传达的重要信息。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Some phone users worry advertisers will take advantage of voice assistants to send ads directly to them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 一些手机用户担心广告商会利用语音助手直接向他们发送广告。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. The spoken web is helpful when one’s hands are occupied.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 当一个人的双手有事时，语音网络会很有帮助。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Some people believe online interaction would soon depend mainly on voice.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 有些人认为在线互动很快将主要依赖于语音。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Setting up a spoken web is by no means an easy task.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 建立一个语音网络绝非易事。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Weather information is extremely important to farmers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 天气信息对农民极其重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Some people are concerned about privacy because their phones are constantly collecting their personal information.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 有些人担心隐私，因为他们的手机不断收集他们的个人信息。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The United States is facing a housing crisis: Affordable housing is inadequate, while luxury homes abound (充裕), and homelessness remains a persistent problem. Despite this, popular culture and the housing industry market happiness as living with both more space and more amenities (便利设施). Big houses are advertized as a reward for hard work and diligence, turning housing from a basic necessity into a luxury.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国正面临住房危机：经济适用房不足，豪宅充裕，无家可归仍然是一个长期存在的问题。尽管如此，流行文化和房地产行业仍将幸福感描述为拥有更多的空间和更多的便利设施。大房子被宣传为对辛勤工作和勤奋的奖励，使住房从基本必需品变成了奢侈品。

paragraphs.sourceText: This is reflected in our homes. The average single-family home built in the United States before 1970 was less than 1,500 square feet in size. By 2016, the average size of a new, single-family home was 2,422 square feet. What’s more, homes built in the 2000s were more likely than earlier models to have more of all types of spaces: bedrooms, bathrooms, living rooms, dining rooms, recreation rooms and garages.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这反映在我们的家里。 1970 年之前美国建造的单户住宅平均面积不到 1,500 平方英尺。到 2016 年，新建单户住宅的平均面积为 2,422 平方英尺。此外，2000 年代建造的房屋比早期型号更有可能拥有更多各种类型的空间：卧室、浴室、客厅、餐厅、娱乐室和车库。

paragraphs.sourceText: There are consequences of living big. As middle-class houses have grown larger, two things have happened. First, large houses take time to maintain, so cleaners and other low-wage service workers are required to keep these houses in order. Second, once-public spaces, where people from diverse backgrounds used to come together, have increasingly become privatized, leading to a reduction in the number of public facilities available to all, and a reduced quality of life for many. Take swimming pools. While in 1950, only 2,500 U.S. families owned pools, by 1999 this number was 4 million. At the same time, public municipal pools were often closed, leaving low-income people nowhere to swim.
paragraphs.translationZh: 生活大是有后果的。随着中产阶级的房屋变得越来越大，发生了两件事。首先，大房子需要时间来维护，因此需要清洁工和其他低薪服务人员来保持这些房屋的整洁。其次，曾经是来自不同背景的人们聚集在一起的公共空间，现在已经日益私有化，导致可供所有人使用的公共设施数量减少，许多人的生活质量下降。以游泳池为例。 1950 年，只有 2,500 个美国家庭拥有游泳池，而到 1999 年，这个数字已达到 400 万。与此同时，公共市政游泳池经常关闭，导致低收入人群无处游泳。

paragraphs.sourceText: The trend for bigger housing thus poses ethical questions. Should Americans accept a system in which the middle and upper classes enjoy a luxurious lifestyle, using the low-wage labor of others? Are we willing to accept a system in which an increase in amenities purchased by the affluent means a reduction in amenities for the poor?
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，更大住房的趋势提出了道德问题。美国人是否应该接受中上层阶级利用其他人的低工资劳动力享受奢华生活方式的制度？我们是否愿意接受这样一种制度：富人购买的设施的增加意味着穷人购买的设施的减少？

paragraphs.sourceText: I believe neither is acceptable. We must change the way we think: living well does not need to mean having more private spaces; instead, it could mean having more public spaces. A better goal than building bigger houses for some is to create more publicly accessible spaces and amenities for all.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我相信两者都不可接受。我们必须改变我们的思维方式：美好的生活并不意味着拥有更多的私人空间；而是意味着拥有更多的私人空间。相反，这可能意味着拥有更多的公共空间。比为某些人建造更大的房屋更好的目标是为所有人创造更多的公共空间和便利设施。

paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Most of us in the entrepreneurial community are blessed — or cursed — with higher-than-average ambition. Ambitious people strongly desire accomplishments and are willing to take more risks and spend more effort to get them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们创业界的大多数人都拥有高于平均水平的野心，无论是幸运还是诅咒。雄心勃勃的人强烈渴望取得成就，并愿意承担更多风险并付出更多努力来获得成就。

paragraphs.sourceText: Overall, this is a positive quality, especially for people trying to build their own businesses. Apparently, if you’re more naturally driven to set goals, you are more likely to succeed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 总的来说，这是一种积极的品质，特别是对于那些试图建立自己的企业的人来说。显然，如果你更自然地设定目标，你就更有可能成功。

paragraphs.sourceText: Actually, this isn’t always the case. In fact, in some cases, extreme ambition may end up doing more harm than good.
paragraphs.translationZh: 事实上，情况并非总是如此。事实上，在某些情况下，极端的野心最终可能弊大于利。

paragraphs.sourceText: One major side effect of excessive ambition is the tendency to focus too determinedly on one particular vision or end goal. This is problematic because it hinders your ability to adapt to new circumstances, which is vital if you want to be a successful entrepreneur. If a new competitor emerges to threaten your business, you may need to change direction, even if that means straying from your original vision. If you have too much ambition, you’ll find this hard, if not impossible.
paragraphs.translationZh: 过度野心的一个主要副作用是倾向于过于坚定地专注于某一特定愿景或最终目标。这是有问题的，因为它会阻碍你适应新环境的能力，而如果你想成为一名成功的企业家，这一点至关重要。如果新的竞争对手出现威胁您的业务，您可能需要改变方向，即使这意味着偏离您最初的愿景。如果你有太多的野心，你会发现这很难，甚至不可能。

paragraphs.sourceText: Few people are successful when they try to build their first brand. Unfortunately, for the most ambitious entrepreneurs, a failure is seen as disastrous, and impossible to recover from.
paragraphs.translationZh: 很少有人在尝试建立自己的第一个品牌时取得成功。不幸的是，对于最雄心勃勃的企业家来说，失败被视为灾难性的，并且无法恢复。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s a clear departure from the intended plan toward the intended goal. For people with limited ambition, however, failure is viewed as something closer to reality. Remember, failure is inevitable, and every failure you survive is a learning experience.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这明显偏离了预期目标。然而，对于志向有限的人来说，失败被视为更接近现实。请记住，失败是不可避免的，你经历的每一次失败都是一次学习经历。

paragraphs.sourceText: Ambitious people tend to be more materialistically successful than their non-ambitious counterparts. However, they’re only slightly happier than their less-ambitious counterparts, and tend to live significantly shorter lives. This implies that even though ambitious people are more likely to achieve conventional “success,” such success means nothing for their health and happiness — and if you don’t have health and happiness. what else could possibly matter?
paragraphs.translationZh: 有野心的人往往比没有野心的人在物质上更成功。然而，他们只比那些没有那么雄心勃勃的同龄人稍微幸福一点，而且寿命往往要短得多。这意味着，尽管雄心勃勃的人更有可能实现传统的“成功”，但这种成功对他们的健康和幸福毫无意义——如果你没有健康和幸福。还有什么可能重要？

paragraphs.sourceText: Clearly, some amount of ambition is good for your motivation. Without any ambition, you wouldn’t start your own business, set or achieve goals and get far in life. But an excess of ambition can also be dangerous, putting you at risk of burnout, stubbornness and even a shorter life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 显然，一定的雄心壮志有利于你的动力。如果没有任何雄心壮志，你就无法开创自己的事业，无法设定或实现目标，也无法在生活中走得更远。但过度的野心也可能是危险的，让你面临倦怠、固执甚至缩短寿命的风险。
